title: Stratified Retention Gatekeeper and Incremental Tombstone Propagation for Console Analytics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a tenant-aware, stratified retention gatekeeper for Console analytics that enforces per-tenant and per-route retention policies, emits incremental tombstone manifests into the streaming pipeline, and provides safe rollback/canary controls for deletions. This ticket covers design, pipeline changes, storage-schema migration, rollout plan, tests, and runbook.
activity_log: 2026-03-01: Ticket created — initial spec written (Aisha). High-level design: classification tiers (ephemeral, standard, legal-hold), tenant overrides, and tombstone manifest streaming.

2026-03-04: Architecture review with infra and security. Decided to avoid snapshot-based bulk delete; prefer incremental tombstones to minimize background load and keep restart-safe idempotent processing (Liam).

2026-03-06: Spike: implemented prototype tombstone manifest format and small consumer that applies tombstones to Clickhouse and object-store indices. Measured 40% lower I/O compared to bulk snapshot delete for our pilot org.
2026-03-07: Security asked for attestation trace for each delete action and KMS-backed shred path for irreversible deletions — added to scope.

2026-03-09: Schema migration plan drafted: add 'retention_tier' and 'retention_expires_at' to analytic_event_v2; consumer will consult retention gating service and tombstone topic. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1987)

2026-03-11: Benchmarks: tombstone fanout consumer processes 10k manifests/minute with <200ms commit latency on staging cluster. Observability spans added for deletion_lag_seconds and tombstone_errors_total. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pipeline/pull/562)
2026-03-12: Began implementing gatekeeper service and canary config. Blocked on IAM tenant-key lookup endpoint stability (ENG-70211 dependency).
acceptance_criteria: Gatekeeper exposes API to evaluate retention policy for a tenant+route and returns TTL, tier, and deletion-mode (soft | tombstone | crypto-shred).
Pipeline emits incremental tombstone manifests with schema (tenant_id, route, primary_keys[], tombstone_time, retention_tier, trace_id).
Consumer applies tombstones atomically and produces audit records; test replay proves idempotence and zero data-reintroduction after restart.
Attestation: every tombstone event is linked to a signed attestation stored in audit-log S3 with HMAC; security review approved the attestation shape.
Canary rollout: enabled for internal org 'redwood-internal' for 48 hours with metric thresholds (failed_deletes < 0.5%, deletion_lag < 30m).
End-to-end e2e tests and a runbook for manual intervention exist (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Console/Retention+Gatekeeper+Runbook).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Long-running backfills could overload Clickhouse. Mitigation: rate-limited backfill agent with shard ownership and progress checkpoints.
Risk: Tombstone manifests could be lost before consumer applies them. Mitigation: use durable Kafka topic with replication factor=3 and consumer checkpoints in ZK + S3 manifests for replay.

Risk: Accidental hard-delete for data under legal hold. Mitigation: gatekeeper enforces legal-hold flag from legal-holds service; crypto-shred path requires HSM key deletion via KMS audit and two-actor approval.
Risk: Query regressions (increased latency) when adding retention gating to read paths. Mitigation: bloom-filter index to short-circuit gated tenants and caching of retention decisions for 5 minutes.
Risk: High customer churn if deletions visible as gaps in analytics. Mitigation: communication plan + visible deletion dashboards and optional retention-export before delete (opt-in).
implementation_plan: 1) Gatekeeper service: API + caching layer + tenant policy store (4d).
2) Schema migration for analytic_event_v2 (2d, backwards compatible).
3) Tombstone manifest producer in ingestion pipeline; produce manifests when retention_expires_at reached (3d).
4) Tombstone consumer: apply deletions across Clickhouse/Tables and produce audit events (4d).
5) Attestation flow and KMS integration for crypto-shred (2d).
7) Backfill agent for historical data with throttling (3d).
open_blockers: Stable IAM endpoint for tenant-scoped key lookup (blocked by ENG-70211) — needed for attestation signing.
Schema migration coordination with downstream consumers (alerts and expectations).
